Learn about applying for programs like TSA Precheck and Global Entry and managing memberships. What are the Trusted Traveler Programs, and how do you apply? The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) manages the Trusted Traveler Programs. These include TSA Precheck and Global Entry . As a pre-approved member, you can use expedited lanes at U.S. airports and when entering the U.S. by land or sea. TSA Precheck is for travelers departing from U.S. airports. Global Entry is for travelers entering the U.S. from international destinations by air, land, or sea. There are also programs for entering the U.S. from Canada and Mexico. To apply, you will need to pay a fee and provide documents proving your identity. Depending on the program, you may need to complete an interview. A set of weights values (the "state of the model"). An optimizer (defined by compiling the model). A set of losses and metrics (defined by compiling the model). The Keras API saves all of these pieces together in a unified format, marked by the .keras extension. This is a zip archive consisting of the following: A JSON-based configuration file (config.json): Records of model, layer, and other trackables' configuration. pages.text: Saving What’s Ours: The Data Rescue Project and the Fight for Public Data – Open Source Initiative Saving What’s Ours: The Data Rescue Project and the Fight for Public Data Part of the Deep Dive: Data Governance Webinar Series The Data Rescue Project (DRP) emerged as a collaborative effort to protect and preserve public datasets that are at risk of being lost, altered, or rendered inaccessible. Our work is based on the belief that public data belongs to the people and that preserving it is a civic responsibility. In this presentation, we reflect on how current threats to public data access expose weaknesses in the systems we rely on to ensure long-term access and stewardship. Our approach is not only technical; it is deeply community-driven. The Data Rescue Project brings together librarians, archivists, technologists, data stewards, and researchers from across disciplines. We recognize that no single organization or agency can solve the systemic problems of public data infrastructure alone. In moments of urgency, grassroots efforts can illuminate what larger institutions often miss: that data preservation is not only about files and formats, but about relationships, trust, and collective responsibility. This talk will highlight coordination among members of the DRP and our partners, including efforts to amplify active preservation work being done by groups like the Environmental Data and Governance Initiative (EDGI) and data repositories such as ICPSR’s DataLumos. In the field of NLP, language models have gone from hundreds of millions of parameters (BERT) to hundreds of billions of parameters (GPT-3) demonstrating significant improvements on downstream tasks. The scaling laws for large scale language models have also been studied extensively in the industry. A similar trend can be observed in the vision field, with the community moving to transformer based models (like Vision Transformer , Masked Auto Encoders ) as well. It is clear that individual modalities – text, image, video – have benefited massively from recent advancements in scale, and frameworks have quickly adapted to accommodate larger models. At the same time, multimodality is becoming increasingly important in research with tasks like image-text retrieval, visual question-answering, visual dialog and text to image generation gaining traction in real world applications. Training large scale multimodal models is the natural next step and we already see several efforts in this area like CLIP from OpenAI, Parti from Google and CM3 from Meta. "The link led me to a fraudulent platform that asked for my personal information, including my bank account," he told the BBC. Etekpo suffered a significant financial loss and began to question the security of his personal data. He had only been online for a few years when the incident happened. As internet connectivity expands in places like West Africa, millions will encounter online risks like his for the first time. How can they be protected? An estimated 2.6 billion people – roughly a third of the global population – currently have no access to the internet. pages.text: Scientific Data skip to main content Home ›› Submit ›› Submission Basics ›› Scientific Data Submitting metadata records for scientific data through E-Link provides the metadata needed to identify scientific data resulting from R&D funding (contractors and financial assistance recipients) or for R&D performed in DOE facilities. Any data that are shared publicly as a result of an approved Data Management Plan or Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMP or DMSP) are required to be announced. To announce datasets through the OSTI STI process, the data must be hosted at a DOE site, DOE Data Center, or other publicly accessible location such as an open repository. The URL (and DOI, if assigned by a repository prior to record submission) must be included in the metadata record. The URL must take the user to a public facing webpage (landing page) which provides a description and metadata for the dataset along with instructions for accessing the data. OSTI does not have a research/scientific data repository, so datasets cannot be hosted, uploaded, or stored at OSTI. The metadata submitted for the scientific data also allows OSTI, via the DOE Data ID Service , to assign digital object identifiers (DOIs) to dataset records and register them with DataCite (for those that do not already have an assigned DOI). This value-added step facilitates visibility, supports persistent identification and long-term discoverability, and improves linkage between DOE's published research results and the underlying data. pages.text: Scotland and Netherlands share series after third ODI rained off - BBC Sport Image source, Cricket Scotland Image caption, There was no play under the shadow of the Wallace Monument Published 1 September 2026 Scotland and the Netherlands have tied their one-day-international series 1-1 after the third match was abandoned without a ball being bowled at Stirling County following heavy and persistent rain throughout the day. The series was arranged at short notice as the Dutch women sought to regain their ODI ranking and avoid a substantial funding cut next year. The visitors won the opening match by 58 runs at Clydesdale, with the Scots securing a convincing nine-wicket victory in a rain-affected second in Stirling. However, it does mean that the Dutch have done enough to secure their ranking and much-needed funds. pages.text: Scotland beat Canada by nine runs to reach World Cup Qualifier - BBC Sport Image source, Ian Jacobs Image caption, Fin McCreath was Scotland's top scorer with 112 Published 7 August 2026 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 tri-series, Forthill Scotland 281-7 (50 overs): McCreath 112; Shirzad 3-55 Canada 272 (49.2): Samra 78; McMullen 3-43 Scotland won by nine runs Scorecard Scotland held on for a nervy nine-run victory over Canada to secure a place at next year's World Cup Qualifier after a tense ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 match in Forfarshire. Fin McCreath's 112, his first international century, helped the hosts post 281-7 at Forthill. Canada hit 50 inside eight overs thanks to Yuvraj Sumra (78), but they fell to 181-7 only for a partnership of 84 by Ansh Patel and captain Saad Bin Zafar to take them close to their target before George Munsey's catch secured Scotland's win with four balls remaining. Scotland are now assured a place at next year's Qualifier as Canada cannot catch them in the League 2 standings. It was the first game of the tri-series, which also involves the United Arab Emirates, to beat the wet weather after two washouts. Grange batter McCreath reached his century from 135 balls in the 47th over. pages.text: Scotland beat Netherlands by nine wickets to level ODI series - BBC Sport Image source, Cricket Scotland Image caption, Scotland made short work of chasing down the Dutch total after a wet morning in Stirling Published 31 August 2026 Second one-day international, Stirling Netherlands 129-9 (32 overs): De Leede 58; Maqsood 3-20, Carter 2-18 Scotland 130-1 (16.2 overs): S Bryce 70*, Carter 33* Scotland won by nine wickets Scorecard Scotland levelled their one-day international series with the Netherlands at 1-1 after a thumping nine-wicket victory in a rain-affected match in Stirling. Sarah Bryce, captaining the side in the absence of her sister Kathyrn, led the way with an unbeaten 70 as the hosts chased down their target of 130 in just over half of their allotted 32 overs, in a game which was originally scheduled for Sunday but fell foul of the weather. The Dutch had enjoyed a 58-run win in Glasgow on Friday and this was another one-sided contest. Darcy Carter made an early breakthrough, taking the wickets of Netherlands openers Phebe Molkenboer and Sanya Khurana, who had piled on more than 150 in last week's encounter. Abtaha Maqsood also took two quick wickets to leave the visitors reeling on 39-4. Maqsood struck again but Babette de Leede made 58 before being run out, while Caroline de Lange added 20 on the way to their total of 129-9. Scotland lost Maryam Faisal after four balls but Carter (33 not out) and Bryce made sure of a comprehensive success. Kirstie Gordon ripped through the Irish top order, the left-arm spinner taking four wickets for just four runs. Abtaha Maqsood claimed three wickets, Kathryn Bryce struck twice and Priyanaz Chatterji picked up her 50th T20 International wicket as Ireland were dismissed for just 71. Captain Gaby Lewis top scored for Ireland on 20, with Georgina Dempsey (12), Abbi Harrison (11) and Jane Maguire (11*) the others to reach double figures. In reply, Darcey Carter (30) and Katherine Fraser (21) enjoyed a 53-run opening partnership, with Kathryn Bryce (7*) and Sarah Bryce (4*) steering Scotland home in the ninth over. Scotland finished second behind unbeaten Sri Lanka in Group A, with Ireland in third place. Netherlands and Pakistan are guaranteed passage from Group B as Zimbabwe and Bangladesh vie for the remaining spot. pages.text: Scotland men's internationals to be shown live on BBC - BBC Sport Image source, SNS Image caption, Live coverage of Steve Clarke's Scotland starts with a visit to Greece Published 7 March 2025 The BBC has agreed an exclusive contract to broadcast live all Scotland men's international football matches in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup. It is part of a wider deal agreed with European governing body Uefa that also includes matches involving Northern Ireland and Wales - the first time the broadcaster has secured live rights for all three of the UK's devolved nations. The contract includes all 14 live Scotland matches, beginning with the first leg of the Nations League play-off in Greece on 20 March and including June friendlies against Iceland and Leichtenstein as well as World Cup qualifiers. pages.text: Scotland propose Titwood venue for 2030 T20 World Cup - BBC Sport Image source, SNS Image caption, Titwood has been the home of Clydesdale Cricket Club since 1876 Published 11 November 2026 Glasgow's Titwood has been chosen as the proposed Scottish venue for the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in 2030. Home of Clydesdale Cricket Club since 1876, the ground is in the Pollokshields area of the city. The board of Cricket Scotland say their decision came following "engagement and consultation with the ICC, ECB and other strategic partners". The 2030 World Cup is being co-hosted by England & Wales, Scotland and Ireland. It will be the first major tournament in Scotland since the 1999 Cricket World Cup when The Grange in Edinburgh staged two group matches. Titwood would require a major overhaul and the next steps include talks with the Scottish and UK governments. Scotland's women met the Netherlands in a one-day international at Titwood in August, while the men played six T20 internationals there in June 2025. pages.title: Scotland women beaten by Sri Lanka in second Emerging Trophy group fixture - BBC Sport
pages.description: Scotland women succumb to a four-wicket defeat by Sri Lanka in their second Emerging Nations Trophy Group A fixture.
pages.text: Scotland women beaten by Sri Lanka in second Emerging Trophy group fixture - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Published 13 November 2026 ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy Scotland 111-8 (20 overs): Carter 62; Masqood 3-18 Sri Lanka 115-6 (18.1 overs): Gunaratne 49; Kumari 2-15, Sandeepani 2-18 Sri Lanka win by four wickets Scotland succumbed to a four-wicket defeat by Sri Lanka in their second Emerging Nations Trophy campaign Group A fixture. Having opened with victory over Papua New Guinea, the Scots batted first against Sri Lanka but were restricted to 111-8 in Ajman, United Arab Emirates. Darcey Carter top scored on 62 runs off 55 deliveries while Sathya Sandeepani and Sugandika Kumari took two wickets each. Sri Lanka's Vishmi Gunaratne amassed 49 runs off 41 deliveries, with captain Harshitha Samarawickrama contributing 24. Abatha Masqood took three wickets, becoming the Scots' top wicket taker in WT20Is, her 77 surpassing current captain Kathryn Bryce. Ten nations are participating in the UAE, split into two groups of five before a Super Six stage to determine the final on 25 November. Scotland play the hosts next, with UAE having opened with defeat by Ireland, who picked up a first win. pages.text: Scotland: Andy Robertson caps it all as he takes King Kenny's crown - BBC Sport Figure caption, You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career By Amy Canavan BBC Sport Scotland in St Gallen Published 16 November 2026 Andy Robertson has become Scotland's most capped men's international after starting in Monday's Nations League defeat in Switzerland to reach 103 appearances for his country. Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he surpassed his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul had stood for 40 years. After moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare. But, in St Gallen, the spotlight shone on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he moves solo at the summit, even if the scoreline was a disappointment. Scott Milliren Scott Milliren is the Director of the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) within the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI). In this role, he oversees a multi-billion-dollar portfolio dedicated to advancing the commercial deployment and scaling of innovative energy, materials, and industrial manufacturing technologies. His leadership supports CMEI’s mission to secure stable domestic supply chains, strengthen American manufacturing, and steward federal resources to provide affordable, reliable, and secure energy for the nation. Before joining OCED, Milliren served as a senior advisor at the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, where he provided strategic guidance on organizational transformation and team development, implementing executive orders aimed at modernizing the commission. Milliren’s career spans more than three decades in the oil and gas services industry, working in both public and private sectors across all segments of energy production, including drilling, equipment manufacturing, production, and completion. Scott Pappano Scott Pappano Scott Pappano currently serves as the Principal Deputy Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). Mr. Pappano has dedicated nearly 35 years of service to the United States Navy as a submarine officer and acquisition leader, including at the rank of Vice Admiral before retiring in May 2025. Throughout his career, Mr. Pappano not only commanded at sea, but shaped the future of undersea warfare and strategic deterrence for generations to come. Pappano served onboard five submarines, including command of USS Buffalo (SSN 715) while forward deployed in Guam. Assignments ashore included submarine tactics development, Navy nuclear power training, defense international security policy, and Navy programming. After selection as an acquisition professional, Pappano served as Major Program Manager for the Strategic and Attack Submarine Program Office (PMS 392). As a flag officer, Mr. Pappano served in some of the Navy’s most critical leadership roles, including Director of the Comprehensive Test Facility, Commander of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Program Executive Officer for Strategic Submarines, and Assistant Secretary of the Navy (Research, Development and Acquisition).
